identity.name: Yan (An Lushan)
alt_names: Yan of An Lushan and Shi Siming

land.text: the Fanyang, Pinglu and Hedong garrisons, 'the area north of the lower Yellow River', that An Lushan held as Tang military governor

predecessors.note: The rebellion began at Fanyang on 16 December 755; An Lushan proclaimed the Yan at Luoyang on 5 February 756, so the dossier counts the rebel zone from December 755.

land.text: Hebei, where the surrendered Yan generals (Li Huaixian, Tian Chengsi, Li Baochen and others) were allowed to stay as military governors; the Lulong, Chengde and Weibo circuits

successors.note: Shi Chaoyi's death ended the state on 17 February 763 (the date his head reached Chang'an); the Hebei fanzhen stayed 'virtually independent for the rest of the dynasty'.

land.text: Youzhou, the former Yan core round modern Beijing, left to the Yan general Li Huaixian

successors.note: An Lushan rebellion page: 'Li Huaixian was made military governor (jiedushi) of Lulong Circuit, headquartered in modern Beijing and covering Youzhou, the former Yan core'.

land.text: Weizhou (Daming), where Tian Chengsi 'took control of Weibo in 763'

successors.note: An Lushan rebellion page: 'Tian Chengsi had full control of Weibo Circuit'.

land.text: the Chengde circuit round Zhen Prefecture, left to the Yan general Li Baozhen

successors.note: An Lushan rebellion page: 'Li Baozhen controlled Chengde Circuit'; the circuit later became the Zhao of Wang Rong.

capitals.name: Luoyang
capitals.note: Proclaimed there 5 February 756; An Lushan 'remained in the Luoyang palace'. Abandoned by An Qingxu in winter 757.

capitals.name: Yecheng (Ye)
capitals.note: After Shi Siming's submission An Qingxu held 'only Yecheng and its surrounding region'.

capitals.name: Luoyang
capitals.note: Shi Siming proclaimed himself emperor on 9 May 759 with Fanyang as his base and took Luoyang in 759; he was killed 'on the way back to Luoyang' in 761 and Shi Chaoyi lost Luoyang in winter 762. Fanyang (Youzhou) is the base city in 759.

rulers.name: An Lushan (Emperor Xiongwu)
rulers.title: emperor of Yan
rulers.note: Proclaimed 5 February 756; infobox reign to 25 January 757 (the Zizhi Tongjian implies the night of 29 January); killed by his son An Qingxu.

rulers.name: An Qingxu
rulers.title: emperor of Yan
rulers.note: Accession dated 30 January 757 in a footnote; killed by Shi Siming in spring 759 (10 April 759 on the rebellion page).

rulers.name: Shi Siming (Emperor Zhaowu)
rulers.title: emperor of Yan
rulers.note: Proclaimed himself emperor 9 May 759 (the rebellion page says 10 April 759); strangled 18 April 761.

rulers.name: Shi Chaoyi
rulers.title: emperor of Yan
rulers.note: Hanged himself in spring 763; his head reached Chang'an on 17 February 763.

correction.text: Fanyang (near modern Beijing) and the garrisons north of the lower Yellow River that An Lushan commanded as Tang military governor

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The rebellion opens at Fanyang on 16 December 755. The page gives no frontier, only the Pinglu, Fanyang and Hedong garrisons 'north of the lower Yellow River'; the whole Hebei plain is the researcher's reading, rounded to the year. No infobox area on any page opened.

correction.text: the Hebei base, Luoyang (taken January 756, the court of the Yan from 5 February 756) and Chang'an with Guanzhong (July 756)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 756 to late 757. Yan held the Yellow River plain north of the river, Luoyang and, from July 756, Chang'an. Tang pockets held out (Yan Zhenqing in Hebei, per the An Lushan page), and the page gives no frontier, so the shape is a generous reading. At the end of 757 Tang retakes Chang'an and Luoyang (ledger 757) and the 758 keyframe takes over. No infobox area.

correction.text: 'only Yecheng and its surrounding region' (An Qingxu after Shi Siming's submission to Tang)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After the winter 757 loss of Luoyang Shi Siming submitted and 'nearby prefectures largely followed, leaving An Qingxu holding only Yecheng and its surrounding region'; the 150 km radius is the researcher's reading of 'surrounding region'. No infobox area.

correction.text: Fanyang and the Ye region again under Shi Siming, plus Bian (Kaifeng) and Luoyang taken in 759

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Shi Siming 'captured Bian Prefecture (Kaifeng, Henan) and Luoyang' in 759 and was stopped at Heyang and Shan Prefecture; he also held Wei Prefecture (Handan). The Hebei region is the researcher's reading of a state whose north-south extent the page does not draw. No infobox area.

correction.text: Hebei: Shi Chaoyi lost Luoyang in winter 762 and his generals turned against him in 762-763

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Luoyang falls to Tang and the Uyghurs in winter 762; Bian (Kaifeng) is not mentioned and is removed at confidence 1 (ledger 762). The shape ends 17 February 763 with Shi Chaoyi's death. No infobox area.

region.text: Fanyang (near modern Beijing), the seat of An Lushan's three commands

ledger.note: 755: An Lushan rises at Fanyang. 'On 16 December, his army surged down from Fanyang (near modern Beijing)'; infobox 16 December 755 to 17 February 763. The Yan dynasty itself is proclaimed at Luoyang on 5 February 756.

region.text: the area north of the lower Yellow River and east of the Taihang Mountains

ledger.note: 755: Hebei goes over to An Lushan. The Pinglu, Fanyang and Hedong garrisons gave him 'control over the area north of the lower Yellow River' (rebellion page); Shi Siming pacified 'the region north of the Yellow River and east of the Taihang Mountains' except 'pockets held by Yan Zhenqing' (An Lushan page). Mirror of the Tang loss of December 755.

region.text: the Yellow River plain between Fanyang, Luoyang and Tongguan

ledger.note: 755: war between the rebels and the Tang opens. The fighting ran over the Yellow River plain between Fanyang, Luoyang and Tongguan until 763 (the Tang dossier's zone).
756: Luoyang falls. 'An Lushan captured the Eastern Capital city of Luoyang on 18 January 756, defeating General Feng Changqing.' Mirror of the Tang loss.

756: An Lushan proclaims the Great Yan at Luoyang. 'declared himself Emperor at Luoyang, establishing a new state of Yan' on 5 February 756 (Lunar New Year); infobox reign 5 February 756 to 25 January 757; era name Shengwu.

region.text: Chang'an and Guanzhong, after Tongguan and Lingbao

ledger.note: 756: Chang'an falls to Yan. On 7 July 756 Geshu Han's army is beaten in open ground and the road to the capital opens; Yan forces enter Chang'an in July while Xuanzong flees toward Shu and Li Heng is proclaimed Emperor Suzong at Lingzhou. The An Lushan page gives no day for the entry and does not say how long Yan held it.
757: Tang retakes both capitals. 'With Uyghur assistance, the Tang Imperial forces recaptured both Chang'an and Luoyang in late 757.' An Qingxu abandons Luoyang in winter 757 (Shi Siming page).

region.text: Fanyang and the Hebei prefectures that followed Shi Siming, except Yecheng and its surroundings

ledger.note: 757: Shi Siming and the northern prefectures go over to Tang. 'Shi Siming submitted to Tang and was made military governor of Fanyang. Nearby prefectures largely followed, leaving An Qingxu holding only Yecheng and its surrounding region.' The page dates this 'late 757 or after'; the Tang ledger has no mirror gain (a gap on the Tang side).

759: Shi Siming takes Kaifeng and Luoyang. 'He captured Bian Prefecture (Kaifeng, Henan) and Luoyang', but 'Tang forces stopped his advance at Heyang (Jiaozuo) and Shan Prefecture (Sanmenxia)' and the front stalemated. The date within 759 is not given. Confidence 2 (reviewer ea-04-x): the Shi Siming page gives no year or season for the capture of Bian and Luoyang; 759 is read from the surrounding narrative and the Tang dossier's 759 loss.

759: Shi Siming takes the Yan throne. 'Shi Siming... enthroned himself as Emperor Zhaowu of Yan' after killing An Qingxu (10 April 759 on the rebellion page; 9 May 759 on the Shi Siming page, with Fanyang as his base): same state, same colour.

region.text: Fanyang and the northern Hebei prefectures, back under Shi Siming

ledger.note: 759: Shi Siming takes over An Qingxu's Ye and 'returned to Fanyang', the northern Hebei circuit that had been under Tang since his submission; Wei Prefecture (Handan) was also taken from the Tang general Cui Guangyuan, with the year given as 759-760.
762: Luoyang falls for the last time. 'Tang forces, aided by the Uyghur Khaganate under Dengli Khan, took Luoyang in winter 762.'

region.text: Bian Prefecture (Kaifeng), held since 759 (page silent on its loss)

ledger.note: 762: Bian (Kaifeng) is lost with Luoyang. The Shi Chaoyi page names only Luoyang and says his attacks on Lu Prefecture and Songzhou failed; nothing opened places Bian after 759, so this is bridging at confidence 1.
763: the rebellion ends. 'Shi Chaoyi chose suicide over capture, dying on 17 February 763, ending the eight-year-long rebellion.'

region.text: Hebei, left to the surrendered Yan generals as jiedushi

ledger.note: 763: the Yan ends and its generals keep their posts. 'Yan generals who surrendered to Tang were allowed to remain as independent military governors'; Li Huaixian (Lulong), Li Baozhen (Chengde) and Tian Chengsi (Weibo) hold Hebei. Shi Chaoyi's head reaches Chang'an on 17 February 763.

wars.name: An Lushan rebellion

zones.text: the Yellow River plain from Fanyang to Luoyang and Tongguan; Chang'an in 756-757

wars.outcome: Tang victory in February 763 with Uyghur help; the Yan generals who surrendered kept Hebei as semi-independent jiedushi (Lulong, Chengde, Weibo).
wars.note: Infobox 16 December 755 to 17 February 763, result 'Tang victory'.

wars.name: Siege and battle of Yecheng
wars.outcome: On 7 April 759 'Shi's forces defeated the Tang armies besieging Yecheng when a storm panicked both sides'; the Tang withdrew south, then Shi executed An Qingxu.
wars.note: The page dates only the battle (7 April 759); the siege's start in 758 is the researcher's reading of 'besieging'.

certainty.note: A rebel zone with no frontier drawn on any page: Tang pockets (Yan Zhenqing, Taiyuan, Suiyang) stayed inside the area and the front moved with each campaign.

sources.title: An Lushan rebellion
sources.note: Dates of the revolt, Luoyang (18 January 756), the Yan proclamation (5 February 756), Chang'an (July 756), the late 757 recapture, the 759 Shi Siming advance, 17 February 763, the Hebei jiedushi.

sources.title: An Lushan
sources.note: Proclamation at Luoyang on 5 February 756, reign dates, Luoyang as seat, his three commands, death in January 757, An Qingxu.

sources.title: Shi Siming
sources.note: Submission of Fanyang, An Qingxu at Ye, the battle of Yecheng (7 April 759), 9 May 759, Bian and Luoyang, Wei Prefecture, 18 April 761.

sources.title: Shi Chaoyi
sources.note: 761 accession, the winter 762 loss of Luoyang, the defections, the 763 death.

notes: Rebel state written for ea-04-x (Cliopatria has no row for it). Pages report no area. Open points: (1) the date of Chang'an's fall is 'July 756' only on the rebellion page and the An Lushan page gives no day; (2) Shi Siming's accession is 10 April 759 on the rebellion page and 9 May 759 on his own page; (3) Bian (Kaifeng) after 759 is not placed by any page (762 loss at confidence 1); (4) the Tang dossier has no mirror for the late 757 loss of Fanyang to Shi Siming's submission nor for Shi Siming's 759 return; (5) the Tang dossier's counterpart strings 'Yan (An Lushan)', 'Yan (Shi Siming)', 'Yan (Shi Chaoyi)' are this one state, slug yan-an-lushan. Gazetteer: 'Ye' for Yecheng and 'Beijing' for Fanyang exist; Fanyang/Youzhou and Hedong are not names in the gazetteer (used only in text).
